Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Preserve right alignment in the legacy flexbox fallback

The new header layout relies on `margin-left: auto` to push `.panel` to the right, but the `flexbox()` mixin also selects the legacy `display: -webkit-box` layout on browsers without modern flexbox support. That layout treats auto margins as zero, and the removed `float: right` cannot position a box-layout child. On those browsers (including older Android stock browsers), the navigation panel now sits immediately beside the logo/topic information rather than at the right edge. Provide a legacy-compatible expanding spacer or retain a working fallback instead of relying solely on the auto margin.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same regression: removing the float-based right alignment and relying on flexbox/auto margins causes the header panel to lose its right alignment in legacy/non-flex contexts. The candidate frames the fallback slightly differently, but it points to the same layout bug.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Apply untrusted-field restrictions to website_name

The new website_name attribute is not included in untrusted_attributes, so it is serialized even when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) suppresses website for an anonymous viewer of a TL0 user. This exposes the otherwise-hidden website hostname (and path for same-domain URLs), and the updated template displays it because it checks website_name rather than website. The include_website_name method does not prevent this: it lacks the required '?' suffix and only checks presence anyway. Apply the same restriction used for website and extend the anonymous/TL0 serializer test to cover the new field.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that include_website_name lacks the required '?' suffix, so Rails won't treat it as a conditional inclusion method. The candidate frames this within a broader untrusted-field concern and omits the string-literal mutation point, but the core serializer convention bug matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB Ruby prevents existing discussions from rendering

The conditional is closed with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby because the trailing `if` has no condition. Rails will raise a template syntax error whenever an existing embedded topic renders this view, so the discussion iframe returns an error instead of showing comments. Close the block with `end`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the invalid `end if` ERB closure and state that it should be `end` to close the conditional.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
RSS entries without a content element abort feed polling

The poller assumes every entry has a non-nil `content` value and calls `scrub` on it. Ordinary RSS entries can provide their body in `description` rather than an Atom-style `content` element, and entries may omit a body entirely. Such an entry raises an exception and stops the entire polling run, preventing subsequent entries from being imported. Support the RSS body fields and handle missing content explicitly.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the poller calls scrub on i.content assuming it is always present, but RSS entries may use description or omit a body, causing a nil/exception that aborts polling. The candidate also calls for supporting RSS body fields and handling missing content, which aligns with the golden fallback to description.

false_positives.candidate:
Imported feed HTML bypasses sanitization

Imported contents are stored with the `raw_html` cook method, whose implementation returns the raw text without sanitizing it. `absolutize_urls` only parses and rewrites URLs; it does not remove scripts, event-handler attributes, or dangerous link schemes. The RSS polling path passes feed contents directly into this method, so executable HTML from a feed is persisted as cooked content and rendered on the forum's origin. Sanitize imported HTML before storing it, including on updates.

Remote retrieval follows redirects outside the allowed host

TopicRetriever checks only the host of the initial embed URL, but `open(url).read` follows HTTP redirects without checking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, therefore bypasses the embedding host restriction and can have its response imported into a public topic. Validate every redirect destination and restrict retrieval to permitted HTTP(S) endpoints before fetching it.

URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths

The rewrite treats every URL beginning with `/` as a path on the article's host. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`; the image rewrite below has the same problem. Conversely, document-relative URLs such as `images/photo.jpg` are left unchanged and resolve against the Discourse URL rather than the source article. This breaks links and images in imported articles. Resolve URLs against the complete source URL using URI joining, preserving protocol-relative hosts.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The new downsize definition replaces the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition immediately above it. Existing calls using `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` now raise ArgumentError. Calls with just width and height instead treat the height as `opts`, which fails when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both calling conventions in a single method or give the dimensions-based entry point a different name.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the second self.downsize definition overrides the earlier width/height version because Ruby does not overload methods, breaking existing calls. The candidate adds concrete failure modes but points to the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Keep attachment validation tied to the configured attachment limit

The hard-coded 10 MB limit applies to attachments as well as images, although only images can be downsized. Sites configured to accept attachments larger than 10 MB now have those valid uploads blocked in the browser. Conversely, attachments exceeding a smaller configured limit are uploaded unnecessarily before being rejected by the server. Apply the expanded pre-downsizing allowance only to images and continue using `max_attachment_size_kb` for attachments.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: a hard-coded 10 MB client-side limit ignores configured per-type upload size settings, so valid attachments can be blocked or invalid ones uploaded before server rejection. The candidate's focus on max_attachment_size_kb is a specific instance of the golden comment's max_<type>_size_kb concern.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage dimensions are not supported by the animated resizing command

For a temporary file ending in `.gif` with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, this call selects gifsicle and passes `--resize-fit 80%`. Gifsicle's resize-fit option requires pixel dimensions in WIDTHxHEIGHT form, not a percentage. Conversion therefore fails, and the loop repeats the same failing operation five times without checking its result. Oversized animated GIFs remain oversized and cannot benefit from automatic downsizing. Calculate pixel dimensions for this path or use a command that supports percentage scaling.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: animated GIF resizing passes a percentage (80%) to gifsicle --resize-fit, which requires WIDTHxHEIGHT geometry, so downsizing fails. Extra details about retries do not change the core issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsizing can permanently remove animation from uploaded GIFs

The upload's original file is overwritten using `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When animated thumbnails are disabled, the conversion reads only `from[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF becomes a single-frame image before it is stored. A setting governing thumbnails should not silently discard animation from the original upload. Preserve animation during upload downsizing, or reject an image that cannot be downsized without losing it.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Handle users without a TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, but the next statement unconditionally reads its notification_level. The unsubscribe URL is not tied to the email recipient, so opening it while logged into another account that has never interacted with the topic causes a server error instead of unsubscribing. This action does not track a visit or otherwise ensure a row exists. Handle the missing record and create the preference through TopicUser.change.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, and the code then unconditionally accesses notification_level, causing a crash. The candidate adds context about the unsubscribe flow but points to the same nil-record issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Do not change notification settings through an unprotected GET

The new GET route immediately changes the logged-in user's notification level, and the unsubscribe action explicitly skips the XHR check. GET requests do not require Rails' CSRF token, so another site can navigate a logged-in user to this predictable URL and silently disable notifications for a topic. Serve a confirmation page on GET and perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST instead.

Record unsubscribe as an explicit notification preference change

Saving notification_level directly bypasses TopicUser.change, which sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed. For users whose topic preference still has a nil reason, TopicUser.update_last_read automatically switches the topic back to tracking once the reading-time threshold is reached, even after this action has muted it or set it to regular. Unsubscribing must record an explicit user change so subsequent reading does not undo the preference.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt

Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not update an @updatedAt field: empty updates leave the timestamp unchanged. Thus this new call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, contrary to its stated purpose. Pass an explicit updatedAt timestamp, or remove the call if this tracking is no longer needed.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: an empty data object passed to updateMany does not trigger Prisma's @updatedAt, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not advanced during cache refresh. The candidate's suggested fix (explicit updatedAt) matches the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Use a sed invocation that works on Linux

The command uses BSD/macOS syntax, sed -i '', which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the environment file, the script therefore leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it updated the file successfully. Subsequent webhook subscriptions use the stale tunnel URL. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle GNU and BSD sed separately, and check that the update succeeded.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: BSD/macOS sed -i '' syntax fails under GNU sed on Linux, so the in-place edit does not work portably. The candidate adds consequences but points to the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache

The cache-deletion mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper does not refetch that query itself, and its onChanged callback is optional and window-focus refetching is disabled. Consequently, a successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and deletion action visible until another refetch or page reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Check the slot's actual end against working hours

The variable end is calculated from slotStartTime, exactly like start, instead of from slotEndTime. As a result, this check permits an event to extend beyond a host's working-hours end. For example, a fixed host available until 11:00 passes a 10:30–11:30 candidate generated from another host's availability. Compare the actual event end with the working-hours boundary so the entire event fits in the host's schedule.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, allowing events to extend past working hours. Wording differs but the underlying issue matches exactly.

false_positives.candidate:
Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts

When an override exists for the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before evaluating busy. An availability override does not make existing calendar events or bookings disappear. For example, a host with a 10:00–12:00 override and an existing 10:00–11:00 booking is now reported as available at 10:00. This affects both fixed hosts and round-robin hosts and exposes conflicting slots for booking. Continue checking busy after validating override availability.

Treat multiple override ranges as alternatives

dateOverrides.find returns a rejecting range as soon as a slot is outside any override on that date. If a host has overrides of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected by the afternoon range, while a 14:00 slot is rejected by the morning range. Valid split-day overrides therefore lose their available slots. The check should accept a slot contained in any override range for that date, rather than reject it for being outside another range.

Do not reject slots outside a different working-hours range

The workingHours.find predicate rejects a slot if it is outside any working-hours range for its weekday. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, every morning slot is outside the afternoon range and every afternoon slot is outside the morning range, so all valid slots are filtered out. This is a regression for personal events as well as team events because this check now runs for their hosts. Determine whether any applicable range contains the slot instead.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Increment the retry counter atomically

Both failure paths write `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before processing the batch. If cron invocations overlap, two failed scheduling attempts can read the same count and overwrite each other with the same incremented value. The reminder then survives more than the intended two failures. Use Prisma's atomic `increment` operation in both failure paths so each failed attempt is recorded.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition where retryCount is incremented from a stale read in both failure paths, and recommend Prisma's atomic increment to preserve every failed attempt.

false_positives.candidate:
Keep retry bookkeeping failures from aborting the entire batch

The new database update inside the catch block is itself unprotected. If a `workflowReminder.update` in the try block fails because the database is unavailable, the catch immediately attempts another update that can fail for the same reason, escaping the loop and aborting the request. A reminder deleted while scheduling is in flight similarly causes both updates to fail. Previously these per-reminder errors were logged and processing continued; now one such error prevents all remaining reminders in the batch from being attempted. Handle failures of the retry-count update separately, including reminders that no longer exist.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

false_positives.candidate:
Group the authorization predicate before returning it without filters

When no service filters are supplied, getBaseConditions() returns the authorization SQL without enclosing parentheses. For team and organization scopes with members, that SQL contains a top-level OR. A raw query composed as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND <date/status condition>` therefore applies the additional condition only to the personal-booking branch, while all authorized team bookings bypass it. The previous Prisma where object preserved the grouping automatically. Return `Prisma.sql` with parentheses around the authorization expression so consumers can safely combine the base predicate with other query conditions.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a literal placeholder

This assignment also runs when credential sharing is disabled. Office365's refresh response schema explicitly allows the provider to omit `refresh_token`, in which case the existing token must be retained. The helper instead supplies the literal string `refresh_token`, which Office365CalendarService merges into the stored credentials, overwriting the valid token. The next refresh then fails and requires reconnection. Preserve the existing token when the response does not contain a replacement.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: when an OAuth refresh response omits refresh_token, the code substitutes the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the valid token and breaking subsequent refreshes. The candidate correctly says the existing token should be preserved.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
The shared response schema strips expiry and other token fields

Using a Zod schema's `.toString()` as a computed property name does not define a wildcard property validator; it creates a literal key such as `[object Object]`. Zod objects also strip unrecognized properties by default. Consequently, a normal shared response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` or `expiry_date` loses its expiry and refresh-token fields. Consumers such as Zoom then calculate an invalid expiry from `undefined`, preventing shared credentials from being refreshed and persisted correctly. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the fields consumers need.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments target the same bug: using z.string().toString() (and optional variant) as computed property keys in the Zod schema. The candidate describes the resulting literal-key/stripping behavior rather than a thrown runtime error, but it identifies the same invalid schema construction and its impact on token fields.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Persist parsed Google credentials rather than the safeParse result

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the complete `safeParse` result, shaped as `{ success: true, data: ... }`, unlike the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call, which returned credentials directly. This result is assigned to `key` and written into the credential JSON. Even with sharing disabled, the first successful Google refresh stores tokens underneath `data`; the next service construction fails because `googleCredentialSchema` expects token fields at the top level. Persist the parsed `.data` instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the refresh parser returns a Zod safeParse wrapper, but the code persists that wrapper instead of the parsed credential data, causing later schema validation to fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize shared responses to the return contract expected by callers

The shared branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, whereas several wrapped refresh functions return already-decoded SDK or Axios results. GoogleCalendarService reads `res.data`, the Zoho services read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch `Response`, regardless of the JSON returned by the configured endpoint. Enabling sharing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt shared responses, or make each caller explicitly handle a common response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the shared credential refresh path returns an unparsed Fetch Response, while callers (Google, HubSpot, and similar integrations) expect decoded token objects with fields like data/accessToken/expiresIn, causing runtime failures when sharing is enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize shared responses to the return contract expected by callers

The shared branch returns an unparsed Fetch `Response`, whereas several wrapped refresh functions return already-decoded SDK or Axios results. GoogleCalendarService reads `res.data`, the Zoho services read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot reads `accessToken` and `expiresIn` directly. None of those properties exist on a Fetch `Response`, regardless of the JSON returned by the configured endpoint. Enabling sharing therefore breaks refreshes for these integrations. Decode and adapt shared responses, or make each caller explicitly handle a common response contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the shared sync path returns an unparsed Fetch Response, but callers expect a decoded object with properties like res.data. The candidate generalizes this to multiple integrations, but it is the same response-contract mismatch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Send the Bigin credential owner's user ID, not the credential ID

The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a Cal.com user ID, but Bigin passes `credentialId`. The helper sends this value as `calcomUserId`, so the parent platform looks up credentials for the wrong user whenever credential and user IDs differ. This can either fail the refresh or select another user's Bigin account. Passing a credential ID also makes team credentials enter the user-sharing branch despite having no user owner. Thread `credential.userId` through this refresh method.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId rather than the credential owner's userId, causing the parent platform to look up the wrong user and potentially fail or select another user's credentials.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured credential source

The newly added Salesforce refresh unconditionally contacts Salesforce using the locally stored refresh token instead of calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Thus Salesforce never uses `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, even when sharing is enabled. Shared credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent platform cannot initialize a Salesforce client. This also performs a direct provider refresh before jsforce is constructed with the old access token, rather than using the token just fetched. Use the configured refresh source and initialize the connection with its refreshed credentials.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that jsforce is constructed with the old access token after a refresh and should instead be initialized with the refreshed credentials. Although it adds broader context about the refresh source, it points to the same stale-token connection bug.

false_positives.candidate:
Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path

The new refresh code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file does not import or declare `prisma`. This causes a TypeScript compilation error and, if type checking is bypassed, a ReferenceError whenever the Salesforce client is initialized. Add the Prisma client import.

Use the actual Zoom app slug in shared refresh requests

The shared refresh request identifies the app as `zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with appId `zoom`, and its installed-app slug is also `zoom`. A parent endpoint keyed by the same app slugs accepted by the credential webhook cannot find the Zoom credential under `zoomvideo`. Send `zoom` so webhook imports and refresh requests identify the same app.

Clear the invalid flag when replacing credentials

Updating an existing credential replaces only its key. Integrations such as Google, Zoom, and Webex mark credentials `invalid: true` after unrecoverable authorization failures. Sending valid replacement credentials through this webhook leaves that flag set, so the replacement does not restore the integration for consumers that exclude invalid credentials. Clear `invalid` when accepting a valid replacement.

Make first-time credential synchronization atomic

The existence check and credential creation are separate operations with no locking or uniqueness enforcement. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app can both find no credential and each create a row. Subsequent deliveries update only one arbitrary row through `findFirst`, leaving another credential stale; calendar integrations can then see duplicate or obsolete accounts. Use an atomic identity constraint/upsert or serialize creation for the intended user/app identity.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await reminder cancellation persistence before completing the request

The cancellation helpers are asynchronous, but their returned promises are discarded by both nested forEach calls and are not included in the final Promise.all. Previously, deletion of the reminder records was awaited. The handler can now report successful cancellation while the cancelled flag or unscheduled-reminder deletion is still pending; in a serverless deployment, outstanding work can be suspended when the response finishes, leaving reminders eligible to send. Collect and await these promises before returning. The request-reschedule handler has the same issue.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: asynchronous reminder cancellation helpers are invoked inside nested forEach loops without awaiting their returned promises, so scheduled reminders may remain active after the handler reports success. It also covers the reschedule path mentioned by the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Rescheduling bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism

Passing immediateDelete=true cancels the old email in SendGrid immediately, even when its send date is days away. These cancellations remain pending until their scheduled dates and consume the same 100-pending-cancellation quota described in this PR. Once the quota is exhausted, deleteScheduledEmailReminder catches the failure without marking the reminder cancelled, so the cron job cannot retry it and the old booking's reminder is sent. Rescheduling needs to persist cancellation intent and use the deferred mechanism too.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments target the immediateDelete=true path of deleteScheduledEmailReminder and the missing database update to the WorkflowReminder record. The golden frames it as a successful SendGrid cancel that leaves an orphaned/unmarked record, while the candidate frames it as a swallowed quota failure that also leaves the record unmarked so the reminder still sends. The wording and consequence differ, but they point at the same code defect: the immediate path does not persist cancellation state on the reminder record.

false_positives.candidate:
Deferred cancellation misses reminders due before the next cron run

Cancellation now only marks a scheduled email as cancelled, leaving SendGrid cancellation to this 15-minute cron job. If a booking is cancelled at 10:01 and its reminder is due at 10:10, SendGrid sends it before the next run at 10:15. That run also deletes the expired reminder record before querying cancellations, so it never attempts cancellation. Reminders close to their send time need immediate cancellation rather than relying exclusively on the cron job.

Isolate cancellation failures and commit each successful cancellation

A single failed SendGrid request exits the entire cancellation loop, preventing every subsequent reminder from being cancelled in that run. Furthermore, the Prisma delete operations collected for earlier successful cancellations are lazy promises and are only executed by Promise.all after the loop; an exception skips that call, leaving all those records in the queue too. A persistently failing batch can therefore block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Handle errors per reminder and await deletion immediately after each successful cancellation.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is converted to lowercase, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. The email validator accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses this restriction and causes an invitation to be sent to the blocked mailbox. Normalize incoming addresses for the blacklist comparison and existing-attendee checks.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same blacklist bypass: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased while submitted guest emails are compared without normalization, allowing uppercase variants to evade the restriction. The extra mention of existing-attendee checks does not change the underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Allow team admins or owners rather than requiring both roles

The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, although either role should authorize managing a team booking. A team administrator who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will therefore receive FORBIDDEN. Use an OR check so administrators and owners can add guests to their team's bookings.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same permission-check bug: isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner are combined with &&, but either role should be sufficient, so the condition should use ||.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees

The uniqueGuests filter only excludes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request with the same new email twice passes validation and supplies two identical attendees to createMany. This can create duplicate attendee records and notifications, or fail the insertion if a database uniqueness constraint rejects them. Enforce uniqueness server-side rather than relying on the dialog's validation.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: uniqueGuests only filters existing/blacklisted addresses and does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted guests array, so createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests therefore sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners disabled them, potentially duplicating workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the same suppression checks.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores EventType disableStandardEmails flags and sends host/attendee emails even when standard notifications are suppressed. The candidate adds consistent remediation details but points to the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates

This handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the logged-in user's identity and credentials. When someone other than the organizer invokes it, those credentials do not authorize updating the organizer's existing calendar event. The database attendee insertion has already completed, so this can leave Cal.com's guest list updated while the organizer's calendar remains unchanged, or fail the request after persisting the guests. Resolve the calendar credentials from the booking organizer instead.

Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations

The handler checks that the booking exists but never checks its status. An authorized caller can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, after which the new email templates send calendar REQUEST attachments with status CONFIRMED and new guests receive scheduled-booking emails. Pending bookings can also reach this action through the existing past-pending edit menu. Reject unsupported booking statuses, or use status-appropriate notification behavior, rather than inviting people to events that are not confirmed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consume backup codes atomically to prevent replay and lost updates

Backup codes are read with the initial user lookup, checked in memory, and then overwritten using an update constrained only by user ID. Two concurrent requests can both read and successfully consume the same code, violating its single-use guarantee. Requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic conditional update or appropriately locked transaction, and only authenticate if consumption succeeds.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same concurrency bug: backup codes are checked and consumed non-atomically, so concurrent requests can reuse the same code and violate one-time semantics. The candidate adds the related lost-update case but targets the same underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup-code login can bypass password verification

Password verification above this branch is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence and never validates that TOTP. A request containing an email, a valid backupCode, and any arbitrary nonempty totpCode therefore authenticates without the account password. This turns a backup code into a standalone login credential instead of a replacement second factor. Ensure the required primary authentication is verified regardless of which second-factor field is supplied.

Expose backup-code recovery for external-provider 2FA logins

When totpEmail is supplied after Google/SAML authentication, the page renders ExternalTotpFooter instead of TwoFactorFooter, so there is no 'Lost access' action and the backup-code input cannot be reached. This affects users who generated backup codes as CAL accounts and subsequently linked an external provider—the account-linking flow preserves their enabled 2FA and codes. Such users cannot use their saved recovery codes after losing their authenticator. Supporting this flow also requires adjusting the credentials provider's external-provider guard, which currently rejects requests without totpCode even when backupCode is supplied.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guard the missing destination before checking its integration

When Google Meet is selected and destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. Reading its integration throws before the intended Cal Video fallback can run. The previous optional access supported this case; bookings with a missing or disconnected destination calendar now fail instead of falling back.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same null-reference bug: destructuring a null or empty destinationCalendar yields an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar, and accessing its integration throws before the intended fallback.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Restore a usable Google calendar fallback for references without an external ID

When externalCalendarId is null or absent, this fallback searches for a destination whose externalId equals that missing value. Valid destinations have string IDs, so the search always returns undefined and events.update is called without its required calendarId. Older references without externalCalendarId can no longer be rescheduled even when the event has a valid destination. The analogous delete fallback now silently targets primary instead of the configured destination, potentially leaving the event undeleted.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments flag the same broken calendar lookup: matching a destination by externalId === externalCalendarId is invalid and yields no usable calendar. The candidate frames the null/absent case and downstream update/delete effects, while the golden comment frames the provided-ID self-match, but the underlying bug is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Do not reverse organization slug assignment based on billing

This changes slug assignment from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while requestedSlug remains conditional on billing being enabled. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive neither slug nor requestedSlug, despite the handler configuring a domain using the requested slug. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately rather than kept as a requested slug. Restore the original condition unless the organization publication flow is intentionally being changed and updated alongside it.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same logic inversion: slug assignment was flipped from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED while requestedSlug remains billing-enabled, causing neither property when disabled and immediate slug assignment when enabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pass each calendar adapter its matching destination

Every host's credential is invoked with the entire destinationCalendar array, but the Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV adapters select only the first entry. For example, with two Office 365 hosts, the second host's token attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar rather than its own. This normally fails; CalDAV can instead filter out all calendars and return success without creating anything. Scope the event to the current destination or make all adapters select by credentialId, as the Google adapter does.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments concern adapters (Office365/Lark/CalDAV) not being updated to honor the new credentialId-based selection that the Calendar interface/Google adapter use. The golden frames it as a signature/contract mismatch (createEvent(event) vs createEvent(event, credentialId)); the candidate describes the resulting runtime bug where adapters pick the first destination instead of the matching credential. Same underlying issue, different framing.

false_positives.candidate:
Retain collective destinations when the organizer has no calendar

The event initializes destinationCalendar to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. Initialize an array and append the other hosts' destinations so those hosts still receive calendar events.

Reconstruct collective host destinations when confirming a booking

Confirmation reconstructs destinationCalendar using only the booking's single persisted destination or the confirming user's destination. The new-booking handler collects other collective hosts' destinations only in memory, and no calendar events are created until confirmation for pending bookings. Consequently, confirming a collective booking still creates an event for just one host. The confirmation path needs to recover the participating hosts' destinations as well; the payment webhook creation paths have the same omission.

Preserve credential IDs on video booking references

Reference creation now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously it preserved result.credentialId for video meetings. The cancellation handler deletes a video meeting only when its booking reference has a credentialId. Newly created dedicated video meetings therefore lose the information needed for cancellation and remain active at the provider after the booking is cancelled.

Cancel recurring events using each host's matching reference and credential

In the allRemainingBookings branch, the resolved credential for the current calendar reference is ignored. Instead, each outer reference repeats a traversal of only the organizer's credentials, and each recurring booking contributes only its first calendar reference. Other collective hosts' credentials fetched from the database are never used, so their recurring calendar events remain scheduled even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's calendar references and resolve the matching credential for each one.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Await the asynchronous reschedule cleanup callbacks

The new async callback is passed to forEach, which discards its returned promise. Errors from the newly asynchronous getCalendar call—including CalendarService constructor errors that previously reached the surrounding try/catch—now become unhandled rejections instead of being logged. The reschedule operation also proceeds without waiting for calendar initialization and deletion. Await Promise.all over mapped callbacks, or use an awaited loop inside the try block. The same conversion in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the viewer bookings requestReschedule mutation needs the same treatment.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: async callbacks passed to forEach are not awaited, so promises are discarded, errors become unhandled rejections, and cleanup proceeds without waiting. The candidate's suggested fix (Promise.all/awaited loop) matches the golden recommendation.

false_positives.candidate:
Defer import calls until an app is requested

Every import() expression in this object executes immediately when the app-store index is evaluated. Consequently, requesting a single calendar or payment provider still starts loading and evaluating all app packages, including unused providers; awaiting one property does not make the other imports lazy. This retains the all-app startup work the change is intended to avoid. Store loader functions (and optionally cache their promises) instead, and invoke only the selected loader.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
